Subject: Badge scanning at Brightline: offline capture + CRM sync

Hi Sofia —

We're running Brightline Fest (12k+ attendees) in late November and need a robust plan for badge scanning where connectivity will be flaky. Primary asks:

- Offline capture on portable scanners (CSV/JSON export) that can be synced after the event.
- Clear consent language on the scanner UI and a fallback opt-in form for people who prefer not to scan.
- HubSpot is our system of record for marketing leads; SFDC is used for enterprise accounts.

Can Redwood advise on the data shape you prefer, dedupe keys you recommend, and how you handle consent text/versioning during ingest? Also curious about latency expectations on bulk imports and conflict resolution if the same badge is scanned twice (scanner level) vs. a later HubSpot import.

Attached: none yet — happy to share a sample export.

Thanks,
Samir

Subject: Re: Badge scanning at Brightline: offline capture + CRM sync

Hi Samir —

Thanks for the context. High-level approach we've used for similar high-volume shows:

1) Device-level CSV export as canonical offline capture (timestamp, badge_id, scanner_id, event_id, opt_in_flag, email_if_present, phone_if_present, ticket_type).
2) Two-pass sync: first pass is a fast ingest into a temporary bucket for dedupe and consent checks; second pass writes canonical records to HubSpot (and optionally SFDC) with an audit log.
3) Consent: include a short opt-in line on the scanner and capture explicit opt_in_flag (Y/N) plus the exact consent copy version id used. This lets us trace which copy a visitor saw.
4) Dedupe: primary key badge_id + event_id; fall back to email when available, with a configurable time-window (we typically default to 24 hours).

Could you confirm: HubSpot is primary for marketing; should we upsert to SFDC only for enterprise domains (e.g., @enterprise.com) or export a daily batch for their CRM team?

Laura/Ben — looping you in for mapping and the offline sync mechanics (handshake, partial writes, retries). I can set up a quick dry-run for Nov 2 if that works.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Field Marketing Ops | Redwood Inference

Samir/Sofia —

Technical notes and an initial mapping attached. Key items:

- File format: prefer UTF-8 CSV with header row. See attached badge_schema_v3.csv for the fields we need on ingest.
- Opt-in copy: include "I agree to receive event-related communications from Brightline Events and Redwood Inference" with a version tag (optin_v1). See optin_copy_v1.docx.
- Offline device behavior: write file-per-hour to local memory and a final consolidated export at end of shift. This reduces partial-write cruft.
- Conflict handling: we recommend de-duplicating at ingest using badge_id + scan_ts, keeping the earliest opt_in_flag positive (if any scan shows opt_in=Y then treat as opted-in unless they subsequently opt out via form).

Attachments: badge_schema_v3.csv (CSV), optin_copy_v1.docx (DOCX)

I'll add a column mapping for HubSpot in the next message.

Laura Bennett

Thanks Laura — this is helpful. A few clarifications:

- HubSpot form ID is the canonical mapping for marketing leads (we've shared the form preview link below). We will also separately push enterprise leads to SFDC using the company domain heuristic.
- BadgeCo will produce hourly CSVs that match your schema; they asked whether Redwood wants a single consolidated file or per-device files with a manifest. Either works for us if you have a preference.

On dedupe & conflict resolution: we generally want the most complete record (email > phone > name). If HubSpot finds duplicates on import it merges based on email, but we want to avoid high-risk overwrites for enterprise contacts.

Samir

Samir/Team —

Attached is the suggested HubSpot field mapping (hubspot-field-mapping.xlsx) and a short playbook:

Plan summary:
- Ingest model: accept per-device hourly files plus a final consolidated file. We will run an ingest job that: validate -> normalize -> canonicalize -> upsert.
- Dedupe keys: email (strong), badge_id+event_id (strong), phone (weak). For enterprise domains, mark record for SFDC upsert and add "enterprise_candidate=true" flag.
- Consent handling: if opt_in_flag=Y we set hs_allowed_marketing=true; include "consent_version" field.
- Backfill / corrections: provide a daily reconciliation run to catch partial-upload issues.

Next steps: 1) Brightline to confirm if per-device or consolidated works best (BadgeCo prefers per-device manifest), 2) schedule Nov 2 dry-run, 3) share sample device CSVs.
